label: Brynjolfsson et al. 2023
finding: Access to the AI assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 14% on average, including 34% for novice and low-skilled workers, with minimal impact on experienced workers.
strength_rationale: Large sample and real workplace data, but a single firm and a single job.
location_in_source: Abstract (NBER WP 31161; later published in QJE 2025)

label: Noy & Zhang 2023
measure: Time to complete a writing task; graded quality
finding: Treated workers finished about 37% faster (about 10 minutes less than a 27-minute control average), and output grades rose by about 0.4 to 0.45 standard deviations. Gaps between workers narrowed.
strength_rationale: Randomised assignment, but a short, writing-only task done in an online setting.
location_in_source: Abstract and results (MIT working paper version; the published Science version may report slightly different figures)

label: Dell'Acqua et al. 2023 (inside the frontier)
measure: Tasks completed, speed, quality (tasks AI handles well)
finding: Consultants with AI finished 12.2% more tasks, 25.1% more quickly, with output quality scored 40% higher. The lowest-scoring consultants at baseline improved most.
strength_rationale: Randomised, pre-registered, and run with real consultants, but one firm.
check_status: Read a summary of the paper only. Open the paper and confirm figures before presenting

label: Dell'Acqua et al. 2023 (outside the frontier)
measure: Share of correct answers on a task built so AI gives a convincing wrong answer
finding: On a task designed so that AI would give a convincing wrong answer, unaided consultants were correct 84% of the time, versus 60 to 70% for those using AI.
strength_rationale: Same randomised design, but this is one task built to trip the AI up, so it shows a risk and not a typical effect.
check_status: Read a summary of the paper only. Open the paper and confirm figures before presenting

label: Lee et al. 2025
finding: Higher confidence in GenAI was associated with less perceived critical thinking (beta = -0.69, p < .001). Higher self-confidence was associated with more perceived critical thinking (beta = 0.26, p = .026).
strength_rationale: Self-reported perceptions from a recruited sample. It shows association only, not measured skill.
check_status: Read the paper PDF (page numbers not checked)

label: Brynjolfsson et al. 2023 (learning)
measure: Worker learning (as described in the abstract)
finding: The authors report evidence of possible worker learning alongside the productivity gains. This is a hint in the abstract, so read the paper before relying on it.
strength_rationale: Described as 'possible' in the abstract, and I have not read the underlying analysis.
